text:
tara: quick alert from zenkai-v2 int8 bring-up on canary  (sorry)  saw a deterministic bidi/apostrophe regression for he->en and en->he samples after the int8-dense quant build. small locale suite shows BLEU -2.9 on he-en pair.
ishaan: can you paste a tiny repro? sounds like punctuation/orientation issue, not just detok whitespace.
tara: minimal repro (he->en):
input: " שלום (2023) — דו"  // Hebrew word + paren + em-dash + trailing word
baseline detok: שלום (2023) — דו"
int8 detok: שלום )2023( 023— דו'  <-- parentheses flipped and apostrophe replaced / stray space before em-dash
ara: whoa. apostrophe changed to ASCII single-quote in the detok, and parentheses orientation flipped. Token ids differ though vocab unchanged.
ishaan: show tokenized ids before/after? could be byte fallback or tokenizer normalization edge with bidi wrappers.
tara: baseline ids: [4102, 88001, 330, 77, 90012]
tara: int8 ids:     [4102, 88001, 330, 90012, 77]  // paren token moved after number causing orientation flip in detok
nora: interesting: the paren token reordering will affect bidi rendering because U+0028 vs U+0029 placement matters for the bidi algorithm. Did we bump tokenizers or change any normalization?
ishaan: build diff: tokenizer code same, but we applied a fast-byte-fallback for unknown bytes in quant path to reduce memcpy. That codepath concatenates raw bytes before token split for batching. Could reorder parentheses in some composed sequences if bytes glue differently.
tara: eval-bot running focused suite now (he-en, en-he, mixed-latin-he)
eval-bot: quick run (n=800 he-en): BLEU delta = -2.9; chrF delta = -1.7; top failure buckets: parenthesis/bracket orientation (38%), apostrophe/quotemark swaps (22%), unexpected leading spaces before em/ndash (15%).
infra-bot: canary runtime note: int8-dense uses kernel set "dense-qint8-v3" on V100-32G as of build 2025-06-02. Logging kernel + packaging hashes.
ishaan: triage plan: 1) run baseline weights through int8 runtime but with old byte-fallback disabled 2) run int8 weights but force legacy tokenizer packer 3) run float baseline on the new runtime to see if detok change is preproc or model.
tara: starting jobs 1 & 3 on canary. also adding a tiny unit test that reproduces the paren reorder with multi-byte sequences + batching.
ishaan: also grep for occurrences where we normalize punctuation differently under quant path (we had a micro-optimization that collapses some Unicode punctuation into ascii equivalents). If present, revert it for RTL locales.
eval-bot: job 1 complete (baseline weights on int8 runtime with fallback disabled): BLEU delta = -0.1, parity with baseline detok preserved.
eval-bot: job 3 complete (float baseline on new runtime with fallback enabled): BLEU delta = -0.2.
ishaan: looks like enabling fast-byte-fallback in the quant pipeline causes the reordering. good isolate. tara: can you push a revert for that micro-optimization on canary and re-run full locale suite?
tara: revert pushed (canary tag zenkai-v2-rc4), kicked off full run.
eval-bot: rerun complete (n=2400 mixed locales): he-en BLEU delta now -0.2; apostrophe/quote swap cases gone; parentheses orientation stable.
nora: great. let's add a CI regression test specifically for bidi-sensitive punctuation sequences and ensure the quant pipeline doesn't enable the fallback/normalize pass for rtl locales. Also add a note to onboarding docs for quantization: "avoid fast-byte-fallback opt in place for RTL-heavy locales".
ishaan: filing follow-ups: PR to revert and harden fallback logic, unit test in tokenization-suite, and an entry in model-onboarding checklist. Holding zenkai-v2 rollout until canary stable across he/ar/ru bidi tests. :white_check_mark:
